full_judgment: 11. We have perused the Annexure-C series along with others but could not find that the same are manifestly paper transactions and the amount put therein are inflated or those document have been manufactured for those cases, because those documents were already among 103 sale deeds produced by the appellant. The certain documents alleged to have been produced by the petitioner do not even show the nominal value of the land in the vicinity for the reason best known to the executants and the average value of those documents also go to show that the value assessed by the Arbitrator is very much meager one. Moreover, the learned Arbitrator in his judgment has elaborately held that the OP No. 1 has claimed that it has considered the sale figure of 103 sale deeds in assessing the compensation of the disputed land but the sale figure is not filed and proved. So, it is not proved that sale figure is correct. It is not also mentioned that who procured this sale figure and on that date. None of the persons who procured or supplied the sale figure has been examined in his case. It is not also proved that the sale figure relates to the land of same vicinity and same facility of the disputed land, Copies of 103 sale deeds have not been filed and proved. The Government ought to have filed the CS Khatian to show that the land relating to the sale figure is of the same description, vicinity and facility of the disputed land. But the Government did not do so. On the contrary, the appellant has filed photocopy of certified copy of 5 sale deeds of the land relating to the same description in the vicinity and facility of the disputed land. The appellant also filed a statement of the sale figure of the 5 sale deeds. Five sale deeds are marked Exhibit-1 series without objection and the statement of sale figure is marked exhibit-2 in favour of the appellant. Perused the certified copies of the appellant 5 sale deeds numbering 6519, 2978, 2979, 6518 and 2733 registered in Fatulla Sub-register Office for the land of the same description, same vicinity and same facility of the disputed land as filed by the appellant. On perusal it appears that lands of the same description, vicinity and facility have been sold at rate of Taka 44,24,000 per acre by these sale deeds PW 1 has stated in his deposition that lands of these 5 deeds are of same description, same vicinity and same facility. The disputed land is situated in an industrial area by the side of Narayanganj Town. Mills and Factories exist in the area from before the acquisition of the suit land, Dhaka-Munshiganj Road runs by the side of the suit land. So, the sale figure as shown by the appellant does not appear to be too much."
